content.question: What are vanishing gradients?
options: Gradients that become exceedingly small as they are propagated back through many layers, so the earlier layers learn very slowly or not at all.
Gradients that become excessively large and cause numerical instability.
Gradients that are manually set to zero before backpropagation.
Gradients that appear only in the output layer of the model.
content.answer: Gradients that become exceedingly small as they are propagated back through many layers, so the earlier layers learn very slowly or not at all.
